target_customer: Developers and retail teams building product search and file retrieval for customers and AI agents, including regulated and high-stakes applications
problem: Teams stitch together parsers, embeddings, vector databases and rerankers to search files and catalogs, and the result is less accurate than it should be; Captain offers a managed, self-tuning API.
business_model: Usage-based API with tiered pricing from free to startup and enterprise plans (per a secondary source)
product_category: Managed retrieval and file search API (RAG as a service) and retail product search

founders.name: Lewis Lien Polansky
founders.background_notes: Company site: came from cybersecurity and runs retail partnerships and developer relations. Employers and education not named.

founders.name: Edgar Babajanyan
education: Purdue (NLP and AI research; degree not stated)
founders.background_notes: Company site: did NLP and AI research at Purdue and builds the lab's search systems.

competitors.name: Google Gemini API File Search
competitors.what: Fully managed RAG system built into the Gemini API handling storage, chunking, embeddings and context injection
competitors.traction_then: Launched November 2025 by a major platform

competitors.name: Ragie
competitors.what: Fully managed RAG as a service for developers
competitors.traction_then: Established startup in the managed retrieval category

competitors.name: Vectara, LlamaCloud, Pinecone Assistant, Vertex AI Search
competitors.what: Managed retrieval platforms compared in a 2026 roundup

technical_complexity.rationale: Tuning retrieval across parsers, embeddings and rerankers per customer dataset is standard but demanding applied ML; the company reports lifting accuracy from about 78% to over 97% on its benchmarks, unverified.

defensibility.rationale: Managed RAG is a crowded category and a big platform (Google) launched a free managed file search; connectors and tuning data give some stickiness.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Google launched Gemini File Search in November 2025, before the YC batch, absorbing the basic wedge; a single blog claims Ragie shut down in July 2026 with users moving to Captain, unverified.

market_need_then: AI agent builders need accurate retrieval over files; multiple managed RAG vendors and a Google product existed, showing demand and competition.

branding.domain_note: Uses captain.dev and runcaptain.com; File Search moved to filesearch.dev; dates not found

identity.visual_style: Open research lab positioning for retail product discovery with blog and open source work

branding.community_and_virality: Launch HN in March 2026 titled Captain (YC W26) Automated RAG for Files

brand_strength.rationale: Generic name shared with many unrelated companies, hard to search; some developer attention via Launch HN.

pivots.to: Search and recommendation models for retail product discovery, with file search split to filesearch.dev
pivots.why: not stated; inferred from the company site, which now leads with retail product discovery

outcome_analysis: Captain is an active Winter 2026 YC company from two founders, building self-tuning file and product search. No outside funding round is public. It entered a market where Google had already shipped managed file search, and the company appears to be broadening toward retail product discovery. Benchmark claims are self reported.
notes: Unverified: EveryDev lists a $130,000 seed from Y Combinator dated September 2025 under Captain Technologies, Inc.; a single aggregator and the standard YC deal, so not a round. A blog claims Ragie shut down 19 July 2026 and migrated users to Captain; single source, unverified. Accuracy figures differ between the YC page (78% to over 97%) and a press summary (about 95%). Pivot entry is an inference from the changed site positioning. Founder employers and education mostly not found.
